title: Lisse O_E-, E- and Qlbar-sheaves and their fibres (Weil II (1.1.1))
statement:
Under the standing convention of Weil II (0.1), let $Y$ be a Noetherian separated scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible, with a geometric point $\bar y$, $\ell$ a prime, $\Qlb$ an algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and for $E$ in the directed set $\mathcal E_\ell$ of finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\Qlb$ [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set] let $\mathcal O_E,\varpi_E,A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ be as in [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. A *lisse sheaf of $A$-modules* ($A$ a finite ring) is a sheaf of $A$-modules on $Y_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] etale locally isomorphic to the constant sheaf of a finite $A$-module [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]; stalks are those of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks].

1. *Lisse $\mathcal O_E$-sheaves.* A lisse $\mathcal O_E$-sheaf is an inverse system $\mathcal F=(\mathcal F_n,t_n)_{n\geq1}$ with $\mathcal F_n$ a lisse sheaf of $A_{E,n}$-modules and $t_n:\mathcal F_{n+1}\to\mathcal F_n$ a map of sheaves of $A_{E,n+1}$-modules inducing an isomorphism $\mathcal F_{n+1}\otimes_{A_{E,n+1}}A_{E,n}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal F_n$. A morphism $u:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ is a family of $A_{E,n}$-linear maps $u_n:\mathcal F_n\to\mathcal G_n$ with $t_n\circ u_{n+1}=u_n\circ t_n$. (This is the full subcategory of lisse objects of Weil II (1.1.1) b): for such systems the pro-object morphisms reduce to compatible families.) Its *fibre* at $\bar y$ is the $\mathcal O_E$-module $\mathcal F_{\bar y}=\varprojlim_n(\mathcal F_n)_{\bar y}$.
2. *Lisse $E$-sheaves.* The category of lisse $E$-sheaves has the lisse $\mathcal O_E$-sheaves as objects, written $\mathcal F\otimes E$, and $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F\otimes E,\mathcal G\otimes E)=\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$, with the induced composition. The fibre is $(\mathcal F\otimes E)_{\bar y}=\mathcal F_{\bar y}\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$.
3. *Scalar extension.* For $E\subset L$ in $\mathcal E_\ell$ with ramification index $e$, and a lisse $\mathcal O_E$-sheaf $\mathcal F$, put $(\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L)_m=\mathcal F_n\otimes_{A_{E,n}}A_{L,m}$ with $n=\lceil m/e\rceil$ (so that $\varpi_E^n\in\varpi_L^m\mathcal O_L$), with the induced transition maps; this is a lisse $\mathcal O_L$-sheaf, functorial in $\mathcal F$, and induces $\mathcal F\otimes E\mapsto(\mathcal F\otimes E)\otimes_EL:=(\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L)\otimes L$ on lisse $E$-sheaves.
4. *Lisse $\Qlb$-sheaves.* A lisse $\Qlb$-sheaf is a pair $(E,\mathcal F)$ with $E\in\mathcal E_\ell$ and $\mathcal F$ a lisse $E$-sheaf, with $\operatorname{Hom}((E,\mathcal F),(E',\mathcal F'))=\varinjlim_{L\supset E,E'}\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F\otimes_EL,\mathcal F'\otimes_{E'}L)$ over $L\in\mathcal E_\ell$ (the 2-colimit of Weil II (1.1.1) d)). Its fibre is $\mathcal F_{\bar y}\otimes_E\Qlb$.
5. *Tensor products.* For lisse $\mathcal O_E$-sheaves, $\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal G=(\mathcal F_n\otimes_{A_{E,n}}\mathcal G_n)_n$ with the tensor products of the transition maps; this induces tensor products of lisse $E$- and $\Qlb$-sheaves (at $\Qlb$ formed over a common $L$). The unit is the constant system $(\underline{A_{E,n}})_n$.

For module-valued locally constant sheaves use the trivialising-datum definition [def-constructible-locally-constant]; scalar extension of module sheaves is sheafified sectionwise balanced scalar extension [def-pod-ring-scalar-extension].

source.place: Weil II, (1.1.1) b), c), d), pp. 146-147 (PMIHES 52): R-sheaves as projective systems with F_J tensor R/I = F_I, lisse when every F tensor R/I is locally constant; E-sheaves as the quotient by torsion with Hom tensor E; Qlbar-sheaves as the 2-colimit over finite E; restricted here to lisse objects and to the cofinal sequence of ideals m^n, as (1.1.1) b) permits

proof.text: Construct the integral scalar-extension diagram at level m by restricting the sheafified balanced extension along O_E to A_{L,m+1}, with source level floor(m/e). The quotient factor and the source transition induce its transition map. Use the scalar-extension adjunction unit and sheafification uniqueness to characterize maps on tensor generators; these formulas prove the inverse-system functor laws and functoriality in the source sheaf.

Scalar extension preserves finite local constancy: it commutes with passage to an etale slice and with constant sheaves, so apply it to a local trivialization. A finite set of module generators maps to a generating set under the adjunction unit; this proves finiteness after scalar extension. Restriction along the quotient preserves finite local constancy.

Induct on the difference of source indices to obtain the source stalk transition kernel and surjectivity for every pair of indices. For the scalar transition, tensor right exactness computes the kernel as the sum of the coefficient-quotient kernel and the image of the source kernel. The ramification ideal identity places the latter inside the target coefficient ideal. Use the canonical scalar-extension stalk comparison and its unit/naturality formulas to transport this tensor calculation to the stalks of the sheafified diagram. This proves the lisse criterion and supplies the required finite-level scalar-extension data.

For a tower E to L to M, injectivity of powers of the nonzero DVR maximal ideal proves multiplicativity of ramification indices; floor division gives the corresponding source-index equality. Construct the scalar associator by uniqueness of left adjoints, and cancel restriction followed by extension along a surjective quotient map. Transport these comparisons through the prescribed finite-level isomorphisms. Their unit formulas give the nested tensor-generator formula. For identity extension, the scalar adjunction unit is an isomorphism on sheaves killed by the quotient ideal. Assemble both comparisons into natural isomorphisms of integral functors. Generator extensionality reduces associativity and both unit laws to composition of index casts, which follows by equality-proof irrelevance.

Rationalize the integral comparison isomorphisms by sending their arrows to 1 tensor the integral arrow. The prescribed pure-tensor scalar-map formula proves naturality on pure tensors, and tensor induction extends naturality to all rational morphisms using additivity of scalar maps and bilinearity of composition. The integral coherence identities prove rational coherence. Apply LocallyDiscrete.mkPseudofunctor to the finite coefficient fields with the prescribed rational categories and functors. Its three coherence obligations are exactly these associativity and unit identities, giving the required coefficient diagram. Expose the explicit integral and rational comparisons and their construction helpers, with their tensor-generator formulas. Define lisseCoefficientDiagramData directly from these canonical rational constraints and their proved coherence laws. Its nonemptiness theorem is then witnessed by this constructed object; do not choose an arbitrary pseudofunctor from nonemptiness, whose statement does not determine the constraints.
